I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the most reliable way for me to use the full year, spread risk, and keep grain output steady. I know this system, I can manage it with the machines and labor I have, and it fits our water conditions better than chasing a higher-risk cash crop. I will stay with improved or hybrid seed instead of old traditional seed because I care more about stable yield, lodging resistance, and uniform maturity than saving a little on seed. On the wheat, I will push management enough to protect tillering, heading, and grain filling, but I will not overdo fertilizer because too much nitrogen brings lodging and disease. On the maize, I will use summer heat and the rainy season, keep nutrients balanced, and reduce tillage pressure after wheat harvest so I can plant fast and hold moisture. I will irrigate when the crop most needs it, spray only as needed to keep weeds, aphids, rust, armyworm, and other common problems under control, and aim for steady production rather than gambling on a complicated plan.
